name: Internet Protocol specification RFC 791
summary: RFC 791 specified datagram addressing across networks, and the ARPANET transitioned to TCP/IP in 1983.
description: The September 1981 DARPA Internet Protocol specification defining datagram addressing and fragmentation across interconnected networks.

date.basis: Date stated by the cited source for this event, not necessarily first preceding work.

events.statement: RFC 791 published a DARPA Internet Protocol specification.

evidence.supports: The specification is dated September 1981 and explains network interfaces, addressing and fragmentation.

evidence.locator: RFC front matter and editor reference
evidence.supports: RFC 791 is an edited protocol specification associated with Jon Postel.

contributions.resource: Agency for which the specification was prepared; this alone does not establish funding.

evidence.supports: The document was prepared for DARPA.

date.basis: Date stated by the cited source for this event, not necessarily first preceding work.

events.statement: The ARPANET transition from NCP to TCP/IP culminated on January 1, 1983.

evidence.supports: The retrospective describes coordinated transition on that date.

events.caveats: The retrospective does not establish simultaneous universal adoption across every connected system.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated event established in the cited evidence for this specific record; not a claim of global priority.

caveats: RFC 791 explicitly replaces RFC 760. It is neither the first internetworking proposal nor a specification of TCP itself; the later network transition concerns adoption of the protocol suite, not necessarily every implementation of this document.

research.note: Independent reader checked RFC text, predecessor notice and participant retrospective of the 1983 transition; no claim of simultaneous universal conversion. Later event and measure enrichment has not yet received independent review.
